review.summary: I reviewed only the text you supplied. The five scoped source files were not included, so I checked the stated evidence for consistency and did not inspect the code itself. Both earlier findings appear fixed. (1) MAJOR, revision-binding browser evidence: there is now a browser re-attestation PASS at sha256:b28c4dcf… It ties the successful run receipt (six journeys, 12 desktop/mobile axe scans, 131 migrations, cleanup) to byte-identical browser runtime files and the E2E spec. It also re-checks all ten WP-17 pinned hashes and confirms WP-17 is still READY. The only file changed after the browser run is WP-09's unit-test file. Because no runtime or E2E source changed, the earlier browser evidence still applies to this revision. The rule that browser and axe checks must rerun if the pinned WP-17 revision changes or loses READY is stated. (2) MINOR, rendered component copy: the guard now covers the three new webinar registration templates. It also renders the shared public Webinar component in its registration, thank-you and broadcast states and checks the actual HTML for LINE, SMS (English and Chinese), automatic sending or reminders, settlement and guaranteed delivery. So the gap at the component level is covered, not just the template data. WP-17 coverage is described accurately. WP-09 relies only on the WP-17 parts that are pinned and READY: one-entry creation, generated pages, public registration, Email verification and synthetic playback. The scheduler and external reminder delivery are listed as still open and not closed by WP-09. The negative-copy guard enforces that no shipped copy promises those open features, and any such promise is called new scope that needs WP-17/provider acceptance. I found nothing in the supplied evidence that misrepresents WP-17 as a whole, and no remaining substantive defects. On this evidence, WP-09 can complete with WP-17's scheduler and reminder delivery explicitly left open. An empty findings list does not certify that tests pass or that the release is ready, and I could not confirm the file hashes or the test assertions myself.
